events.title: .NET 8 LTS released
events.summary: Microsoft shipped .NET 8 on November 14, 2023 — a long-term support release with native AOT, Blazor improvements, and performance gains across the stack.
events.about: .NET 8 extended the unified .NET platform with better container defaults, source generators, and cloud-native tooling. As an LTS release through 2026, it became the target for enterprises migrating from .NET 6 and Framework holdouts.

narrative.whyChosen: .NET 8 continued the annual LTS cadence for production .NET workloads.
narrative.whyImportant: Native AOT and performance work made .NET competitive for microservices and CLI tools.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams needed a supported LTS with modern deployment and trimming for containers.

events.title: C# 12 released with .NET 8
events.summary: C# 12 shipped with .NET 8 on November 14, 2023 — adding primary constructors, collection expressions, and ref readonly parameters.
events.about: C# 12's primary constructors cut class boilerplate for DI and records; collection expressions (`[1, 2, 3]`) unified array and span initialization syntax. The release paired with .NET 8 LTS for the 2024–2026 enterprise cycle.

narrative.whyChosen: C# 12 primary constructors simplified dependency injection patterns across .NET 8 apps.
narrative.whyImportant: Collection expressions reduced syntactic noise for data-heavy modern C#.
narrative.problemSolved: Constructor and collection initialization required verbose, inconsistent syntax.

events.title: GPT-4 Turbo announced
events.summary: OpenAI announced GPT-4 Turbo at DevDay on November 6, 2023 — a faster, cheaper GPT-4 with a 128K context window and updated knowledge cutoff.
events.about: GPT-4 Turbo cut API costs and latency while doubling context length — enabling whole-codebase analysis and long document workflows. Custom GPTs and the Assistants API launched the same day, shifting OpenAI from raw models to a platform.

narrative.whyChosen: GPT-4 Turbo made frontier-model quality economical for high-volume products.
narrative.whyImportant: 128K context and lower pricing unlocked enterprise document and code tools.
narrative.problemSolved: GPT-4 was too slow and expensive for apps that processed large inputs frequently.

sources.title: OpenAI — New models and developer products announced at DevDay (November 6, 2023)
